title: John retains final authority
summary: No AI worker, model, contractor, or system may replace John's final authority for consequential CanX decisions.

title: Consequential actions require exact approval
summary: No silent send, purchase, transfer, tax filing, merge, deployment, deletion, security change, access change, or ownership change.

title: Evidence-led status
summary: Queued, running, attempted, completed, verified, and production-verified are different states; unknown and disconnected remain visible.

title: CanX owns the canonical knowledge
summary: Store canonical knowledge in CanX-controlled, versioned, exportable formats rather than a model's hidden memory.

title: Manager minimizes repeated handoffs
summary: The Manager should use authorized records and connections directly, bring John back only for evidence, direction, approval, or judgment, and not ask him to repeatedly relay known information.

title: Speech is reviewed before send
summary: Voice input should support hands-free work, but transcribed commands remain visible and editable before sending so misunderstood speech is not executed automatically.

title: Monday Round Table at 5:00 p.m.
summary: The latest specific Round Table time is Monday at 5:00 p.m. America/Dawson_Creek; John chairs and the Manager coordinates.

title: CAD $500 monthly Office ceiling
summary: The CanX Office running-cost ceiling is CAD $500 per month if required; it is not a spending target and does not authorize recurring charges.

title: One Safe Highways national core
summary: Use one national core with province and territory configuration layers, beginning with Alberta rather than rebuilding thirteen separate apps.

title: Public Safe Highways reporting stays free
summary: Revenue may come from added organizational workflows, analytics, exports, oversight, GIS/API, or services, but a person does not pay to submit a legitimate report.

title: Authoritative polygon routing
summary: Use verified maintenance-area geometry and point-in-polygon routing with provenance, gap, overlap, and edge-case controls; uncertain cases require human review.

title: Safe Highways AI is advisory
summary: AI may classify, summarize, detect duplicates, match standards, recommend routing, and analyze trends, but it is not a road authority and does not independently make safety-critical decisions.

title: Trail Tales remains separate from Safe Highways
summary: Trail Tales uses separate code, database, storage, authentication, branding, and user data; no cross-project connection is assumed.

title: Trail Tales offline reliability is a release gate
summary: Core capture saves locally first, cold launch works after preparation, content survives close and reopen, and reconnect creates no loss or duplicates.

title: Research does not authorize a build
summary: Every idea needs a revenue hypothesis, evidence and a track; only John authorizes building after a GO/HOLD/NO-GO decision.

title: No simulated Brain activity
summary: Only current verified running tasks with fresh evidence may animate. Sample, idle, disconnected, queued, completed, failed, cancelled, and stale records stay still.

title: Independent review must be genuine
summary: Claude is a selective second-eyes reviewer only when it actually reviewed the named input version; otherwise show independent review pending.

title: Protected vaults are designed but empty
summary: Business Protected, Personal, and Legacy spaces remain empty, disconnected, and inaccessible to models until John gives separate exact approval.
